correctness.rationale: On upsets, composing the ordinary Heyting pseudocomplement with the co-Heyting supplement gives F(U)=up(down(U)). A point belongs after one step exactly if it shares a lower bound with some point in U. Thus reflexive common-lower-bound graph expansion gives F^j, and its components agree with the comparability graph (each graph edge is a comparability walk of length at most two; comparables are adjacent). Closure fills exactly the reached components, and the fixed sets are precisely the upsets with upset complements. If k>0 is the last strict growth index in the sense of k steps, a shortest length-k path from U has k distinct nonminimal vertices before its last vertex: starting at a minimal vertex would make the next vertex also belong to U, and an internal minimal vertex would supply a shortcut. Choose a minimal lower bound for each edge; finiteness makes such a choice possible and minimality among common lower bounds implies minimality in the poset. Repetition of a chosen bound would again shortcut the path. These k new distinct vertices prove n>=2k. As an independent graph check, any shortest comparability path from U must first descend (an ascending step stays in U) and alternate directions (two successive steps in one direction shortcut by transitivity). Grouping descending-ascending pairs, with a solo last descending edge if needed, shows that distance from U in the common-lower-bound graph is the ceiling of half the comparability distance: the reverse inequality is immediate by expanding each common-lower-bound edge into at most two comparability edges. In the height-two fence the comparability graph is a path of 2k vertices from b_0 to a_(k-1), hence that endpoint takes k steps. An added isolated vertex does not alter the reached component; n=1 and U empty are fixed from the start.
residual_risks: The frozen checker was inspected, not executed. It enumerates naturally labelled poset encodings up to six points with repetitions and tests a finite fence range; the proof is what applies to arbitrary finite n. The distances in the two graphs are not generally identical: incomparable maxima sharing a minimum give distances 1 and 2 from one to the other.

evidence: The alternating-nuclei result gives floor(h/2)+1 for composing two arbitrary nuclei on a finite Heyting frame of height h. Gopaulsingh studies successive lower and upper approximations using two equivalence relations (e.g. L2 L1), including reconstruction problems.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A size bound on this alternating pair of negations is not the height bound for alternating two nuclei: the negations are antitone, not nuclei; even the composite cannot be an alternating product of two nuclei on the same height-two frame for unbounded k, since the cited height bound would be uniform. Equivalence-class approximations act on a different carrier and are not identified with the mixed up/down closure by the inspected results.

evidence: A comparability-component theorem only decides eventual membership and does not count individual F-steps. Counting ordinary edges without the alternation property gives only n-1, and an example matching floor(n/2) must start at an upset.

The finite bound follows by the structural step of compressing a shortest descending/ascending zigzag from an upset into common-lower-bound moves, or by counting disjoint minimal edge witnesses and nonminimal vertices. The extremal fence realizes the maximum under the upset constraint.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The mathematics is elementary but the additional metric argument and an admissible extremizer are needed: neither the least-updownset formula nor the adjacent exact results imply the whole sharp theorem under their stated hypotheses.

evidence: Tasiou's implications U->V=(down(U\V))^c and U<-V=up(U\V) give the composite exactly as up(down(U)); Definition 2.1 gives the same comparability-component closure via zigzags.

Stell–Worboys give the general co-Heyting supplement. The same-day spectra record covers static excluded-middle/double-negation formulas and uses comparability components.

The compared statements do not identify the exact iteration count from metric distance or state the extremal finite carrier result. Composing via the order dual does not change that question.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the sharp number of iterations for this particular composite on finite posets, with start-dependent graph distances and a matching fence at each size. The bi-Heyting operations, their up/down-set expression, comparability components and the eventual least updownset are established ingredients, not the basis of the pass.
residual_risks: The external keyword search did not return a materially useful match and has no negative evidential weight. A prior finite zigzag or finite-topological formulation could have been missed. The pass is a best-of-knowledge decision from the compared statements, not a priority certification.

value.rationale: The existing component description says where closure ends but not how many mixed-negation layers are needed to get there. The theorem gives that cost from the start set and a sharp worst case using only carrier size, with no saving from restricting to height two. In particular a fence misses its terminal minimum before the predicted step, giving an explicit minimal-size obstruction to faster uniform convergence. This is a bound on the specified iteration, not a claim about the expressive depth of all possible formulas.
residual_risks: No bound for infinite carriers or for arbitrary other composites is established.
